stories.story_title: UAA EEG research moves from public datasets to locally collected signals
stories.summary_2_sentences: UAA announced acquisition of a Wearable Sensing DSI-24 dry EEG for its AI and Robotics Lab. Reading-related cognitive-state estimation and analysis of brain activity and eye movements during programming are planned research applications.
stories.why_it_matters_to_alaskans: Anchorage students gain equipment to collect task-specific data, with interdisciplinary collaboration envisioned.

short_quote.text: so I’m excited to be able to collect my own data for my own tasks
short_quote.speaker: Vadim Egorov, UAA graduate student

stories.verified_status: Equipment acquired; students and faculty trained; photograph documents Egorov viewing his EEG signals. Funding came from the Educational Legacy Fund.
evidence_boundaries: Both named studies are planned. No completed programming experiment or reading-study findings reported.
No accuracy, classification performance, sample size, patient outcome, model architecture, cost or recruitment date reported.
The source measures scalp electrical activity; it does not establish direct measurement of thoughts, comprehension or intention.
Manufacturer manual PDF page 64 explicitly limits the device to research rather than medical diagnosis or clinical use. Do not depict a treatment or diagnostic deployment.
Manufacturer lists QStates cognitive classification as compatible software; UAA does not say it acquired or uses QStates. Do not attribute this algorithm or vendor performance claims to UAA.
stories.story_fuel: A person creates the signal; a headset makes it observable; a research question determines what a model must learn. The causal change is access to locally collected data. Show planned experiments as unanswered questions.
stories.local_sentiment: Documented enthusiasm from Egorov and faculty; institutional accounts only. No independently reported community or participant reaction located.
stories.recommendation: Lead. Clear date and explicit AI research connection; visually distinct from recent natural-environment films.

stories.story_title: Lost Lakes platform follows disappearing Arctic water, including Northwest Alaska
stories.summary_2_sentences: AWI announced its Lost Lakes platform on September 10. Satellite-derived water-area records can help distinguish persistent drainage from temporary fluctuations across Arctic permafrost regions.
exact_figures: Around 4 million Arctic lakes in platform
Just under 10,000 lakes lost sizeable area or disappeared since 2016 (Arctic-wide)
Researchers' August 26 account identified around 30 lakes affected by drainage in Northwest Alaska during June and July 2026

short_quote.text: Local people, who spend a lot of time in this landscape, are usually the first to notice its constant ongoing change
short_quote.speaker: Ingmar Nitze

stories.ai_boundary: AWI describes a numerical satellite index for Lost Lakes, and separately the broader Permafrost Discovery Gateway AI initiative. Researcher-authored August account explicitly discusses AI image analysis. Do not invent a Lost Lakes neural-network architecture or accuracy statistic.
stories.story_fuel: A lake can survive centuries and empty within hours; the information can arrive before a journal paper.
stories.local_sentiment: Researcher emphasizes local observers' existing knowledge. No direct Alaska resident reaction found.
stories.confidence: high for platform; medium for precise AI mechanism
stories.recommendation: Backup; resembles September 10 remote-sensing/permafrost imagery. Live dashboard could not be fetched by web tool.

other_verified_leads.title: Charting the Future of Fisheries-Independent Surveys
other_verified_leads.finding: Alaska Fisheries Science Center-led framework urges calibration and parallel testing of autonomous vehicles, cameras, acoustics and eDNA alongside legacy surveys. Physical fish samples still supply age, diet and condition information.
other_verified_leads.hold_reason: Alaska.AI already discussed this source in the September 6 site article Run Both Instruments, or Lose the Record. Robotics is real; new AI model or performance result is not established.
